title: More than 1,500 people displaced after typhoon remnants devastate Alaskan villages
summary: At least one person was killed and two were missing after weekend storm battered two Alaska Native communities More rain and wind were forecast Wednesday along the Alaska coast where two tiny villages were decimated by the remnants of Typhoon Halong and officials were scrambling to find shelter for more than 1,500 people driven from their homes. The weekend storm brought high winds and surf that battered the low-lying Alaska Native communities along the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta in the south-western part of the state, nearly 500 miles (800km) from Anchorage.
